correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts both hub states. With the hub blue, the process on the path is exactly ordinary path zero forcing, and the published endpoint-or-adjacent-pair criterion gives necessity and sufficiency. With the hub white, no path-to-path force can occur before the hub is forced; the hub can be the first forced vertex exactly from a selected boundary pair or selected consecutive triple. Each such pattern leaves an endpoint or adjacent pair on the path after the hub turns blue, so forcing completes. The two disjoint regimes yield the polynomial. The packaged verifier independently checks every subset for \(3\le m\le10\), every coefficient, and all minimum sets.

value.rationale: Fan graphs are a canonical join family obtained by adding one universal vertex to a path, and zero forcing polynomials were introduced specifically to refine scalar zero forcing information to all cardinalities. The theorem identifies a sharp dynamical split created by the hub: the selected-hub case inherits the path criterion, while the unselected-hub case is governed by boundary pairs and length-three runs. The resulting transfer-matrix enumerator and complete minimum-set classification give a natural exact benchmark that is materially stronger than the elementary scalar equality \(Z(F_m)=2\).
